final2.subject: physical-education-ocr
final2.text: Type — the method of training used. Type must align with the principle of specificity: a long-distance runner should use continuous training; a boxer should use circuit training with punching drills and HIIT; a gymnast needing flexibility should include stretching within a structured warm-up and cool-down. Choosing the wrong type of training may improve a general component of fitness without translating to sport-specific performance gains.

final2.subject: computer-science
final2.text: More cores only help if the software is written to split its work into parts that can run at the same time. Some tasks are sequential — each step depends on the result of the last — and cannot be shared out, so they run no faster on eight cores than on one. Cores also share resources such as memory, so doubling the number of cores rarely doubles real-world performance.

final2.subject: citizenship-aqa
final2.text: A juror is a citizen selected at random from the electoral register to serve on a jury in a Crown Court trial. Jury service is a legal obligation — most adults on the electoral register between the ages of 18 and 75 are eligible to be called and must attend unless they have a valid reason to be excused. The jury of twelve hears evidence presented by both the prosecution and the defence, and then deliberates in private to reach a verdict of guilty or not guilty.

final2.subject: classical-civilisation-ocr
final2.text: The baths served social and political purposes as well as hygienic ones. Local politicians and emperors sponsored free bathing days as a form of public generosity (euergetism). Controlling access to luxuries like the baths was one way the Roman elite maintained their status and popularity.

final2.subject: electronics-eduqas
final2.text: A block diagram represents a complete system as a chain of labelled rectangles. Each block is a subsystem; arrows show the direction of signal flow. The signal chain for a PA system follows a logical sequence from transducer to output.

final2.subject: astronomy-edexcel
final2.text: Optical telescopes gather visible light — but the universe radiates across the entire electromagnetic spectrum. Hot gas emits X-rays; cold dust clouds glow in infrared; accelerating electrons in magnetic fields produce radio waves. To build a complete picture of the cosmos, astronomers have built telescopes sensitive to radio waves, infrared, ultraviolet, X-rays and gamma rays. Each wavelength window reveals phenomena invisible to all others.

final2.subject: history-ocr
final2.text: By 1520 the pre-Reformation Church was woven into every part of English life. It was the institution people were born into, married within and buried by. Parish churches stood at the centre of every village and town. The Church owned roughly one-fifth of all land in England and collected income through tithes — a tax of one-tenth of a parishioner’s produce — as well as fees for baptisms, marriages and burials.

final2.subject: history-eduqas
final2.text: Frederick Lewis Allen’s Only Yesterday (1931) presented the 1920s as a decade of social liberation and economic optimism. Lynn Dumenil’s The Modern Temper (1995) argued that the decade was equally characterised by cultural conflict, racial violence, nativist anxiety and the fragility of prosperity. These two interpretations represent the core debate about the decade’s real character.

final2.subject: geology-eduqas
final2.text: A different type of convergent boundary forms when two continental plates collide. Neither plate is dense enough to subduct, so instead the crust is crumpled and thickened into a mountain belt. This is how the Himalaya formed: the Indian part of the Indo-Australian Plate has been colliding with the Eurasian Plate for roughly 50 million years, producing the highest mountain range on Earth. The collision generates intense compressional stress, folding and thrusting the rocks into the complex structures you studied in the first lessons of this unit.

final2.subject: engineering-aqa
final2.text: Metal sintering (also called selective laser sintering or SLS when applied to metals, or DMLS — Direct Metal Laser Sintering) spreads a thin layer of metal powder across the build platform and a laser selectively fuses the particles. Unfused powder acts as its own support structure and is recycled after the build. The result is a fully dense metal component with mechanical properties close to those of a traditionally machined part.

final2.subject: economics-aqa
final2.text: For the government, scarcity shows up as a finite tax revenue. The UK government must decide how to divide its spending between the NHS, schools, defence, infrastructure and social care. Spending £1 billion more on hospitals means £1 billion less available for roads or housing. These trade-offs are at the heart of political debate — but they are ultimately driven by the underlying economic reality of scarcity.

final2.subject: geography-aqa
final2.text: The Arctic is warming at roughly twice the global average rate — a process called Arctic amplification. As sea ice melts, the dark ocean surface absorbs more heat than the reflective white ice did, accelerating warming further (a positive feedback loop). Permafrost thaw releases methane — a greenhouse gas 80 times more powerful than CO₂ over 20 years — which accelerates global warming in turn. Polar bears depend on sea ice to hunt seals; as the ice-free season lengthens, bears have less time to feed, lose condition and raise fewer cubs. Scientists project that summer Arctic sea ice could disappear entirely before 2050 if current trends continue.

final2.subject: drama-aqa
final2.text: The playwright provides the raw material: the script, the dialogue, the stage directions, and the characters. Once a playwright hands over a script, they typically have no further creative authority in a professional production — the director interprets the text as they see fit. This is why two productions of the same play can look and feel entirely different.

final2.subject: latin-eduqas
final2.text: Some enslaved people held a peculium — savings or property that, in strict law, still belonged to the owner, but which the enslaved person was treated as controlling day to day. An enslaved person could build up a peculium through skilled work, trade or careful saving, and eventually use it to buy their own freedom outright. In practice, few enslaved people had the resources to do this quickly, so most who gained freedom this way had built up their savings over many years of trusted service.

final2.subject: food-preparation-and-nutrition-eduqas
final2.text: Time links directly to temperature. Bacteria left in the danger zone for extended periods reach dangerous levels. The general food-hygiene principle of “the two-hour rule” — not leaving prepared food at room temperature for more than two hours — reflects this. After two hours in warm conditions, bacterial counts in high-risk foods can reach levels that cause illness.

final2.subject: it-ocr
final2.text: Every time you tap a screen, speak a command, click a mouse button or press a key, you are using an interaction method — a way of sending instructions to a device. The exam requires you to know the five named interaction methods, their advantages and disadvantages, and which contexts each one suits. This topic is one of the least well-answered despite the methods being listed directly in the specification. This lesson treats them as the central topic and builds in the vocabulary to justify each choice in a scenario.

final2.subject: engineering-eduqas
final2.text: Tool steel has a higher carbon content than mild steel and can be hardened through heat treatment processes such as quenching (rapid cooling). The result is a very hard material that holds a sharp cutting edge. This makes it suitable for cutting tools, drills, punches, dies and blades. The trade-off is that tool steel is more brittle than mild steel — it can fracture under impact loading rather than deforming. It is generally not welded in service because welding disrupts the heat-treated microstructure.

final2.subject: sociology-aqa
final2.text: Social stratification refers to the system by which society ranks categories of people in a hierarchy. In every known human society, some groups enjoy greater wealth, status and power than others. Sociologists explain this unequal ordering in very different ways, depending on their perspective. This lesson examines the functionalist explanation of why stratification exists, before considering how rival perspectives challenge it.

final2.subject: media-studies-aqa
final2.text: Not everyone views media globalisation as neutral or beneficial. Critics have argued that the dominance of globally operating media organisations — many of which are based in a small number of wealthy countries — can produce a form of cultural influence that privileges certain values, aesthetics and narratives over others. This idea is sometimes linked to the concept of cultural imperialism: the argument that media globalisation is not just economic but carries cultural weight, shaping what audiences worldwide see as normal, desirable or prestigious.

final2.subject: citizenship-aqa
final2.text: Rights are entitlements that citizens hold, such as the right to free speech, the right to a fair trial, and the right to vote. In the UK, these are protected by the Human Rights Act 1998, which incorporates the European Convention on Human Rights into domestic law. Responsibilities are the duties that citizens owe in return — obeying the law, paying taxes, and respecting the rights of others. Rights and responsibilities are two sides of the same coin: a democracy functions only when citizens exercise both.

final2.subject: health-social-care-ocr
final2.text: The spec lists eight specific measures. Hair tied back or covered prevents loose hair from falling into wounds, food or onto vulnerable service users. Open wounds covered is essential because an uncovered wound on a care worker can harbour infection and introduce bacteria to a service user through direct contact. No jewellery is required because jewellery, particularly rings with stones, can harbour bacteria in hard-to-clean crevices; rings also puncture disposable gloves. No nail polish is required because chipped or cracked nail polish can flake into food or onto equipment, and the raised surface around polished nails makes thorough handwashing harder.

final2.subject: economics-aqa
final2.text: The tertiary sector now generates the vast majority of UK GDP and employment. Financial services, retail, hospitality, education and healthcare are among the largest employers. Cities like London are global centres for banking and insurance — activities that did not even exist in their modern form a century ago.

final2.subject: separate-sciences-ocr
final2.text: Biodiversity refers to the variety of species present. High biodiversity makes ecosystems more resilient: if one species declines, others can partially fill its role. Human activities such as deforestation, intensive farming, pollution and over-hunting reduce biodiversity. Conservation programmes — protected habitats, captive breeding, seed banks — aim to preserve biodiversity for ecological stability and future generations.

final2.subject: computer-science-eduqas
final2.text: A digital image is made up of a grid of tiny coloured squares called pixels (short for “picture elements”). When a computer stores a bitmap image, it records the colour of every single pixel as a binary number. The whole image is then nothing more than a long sequence of binary codes — one for each pixel, row by row from top-left to bottom-right.

final2.subject: design-technology-eduqas
final2.text: Understanding context involves identifying the end user — not just anyone who might buy the product, but the specific group whose life will be improved by it. A wheelchair designed without input from wheelchair users will almost certainly fail in ways a desk-based designer could never anticipate. This is why designers spend time gathering evidence before they generate ideas.

final2.subject: french-aqa
final2.text: Telling the time: Il est huit heures. — It is 8 o’clock. Il est huit heures et quart. — It is quarter past 8. Il est huit heures et demie. — It is half past 8. Il est neuf heures moins le quart. — It is quarter to 9. Il est midi. — It is midday. | Il est minuit. — It is midnight. 24-hour clock: Il est treize heures quinze. — It is 13:15.

final2.subject: spanish-aqa
final2.text: This is a popular exam topic. You need to explain the qualities of an ideal friend and give reasons. Use un buen amigo debe ser (a good friend should be) or para mí, lo más importante es (for me, the most important thing is) to structure your answer.

final2.subject: l12-retail-business
final2.text: Seasonal peaks are a double-edged sword. The Christmas period offers the opportunity to generate the majority of annual profit in a matter of weeks — but a retailer that is poorly prepared risks running out of key products, losing customers to competitors, suffering website crashes from surging online traffic, or being unable to dispatch orders on time due to insufficient warehouse and delivery staff. A warm summer can boost sales of seasonal products dramatically for clothing and garden retailers, but an unexpectedly cool summer can leave them overstocked with swimwear and barbecue equipment. The risk of holding too much seasonal stock is that it must be sold at heavily discounted prices after the season ends, reducing profitability. Managing this balance — ordering enough to satisfy demand without over-ordering — is one of the central challenges of retail buying and planning.

final2.subject: film-studies-eduqas
final2.text: Blinded by the Light (2019) was directed by Gurinder Chadha, adapting a screenplay co-written with Sarfraz Manzoor and Paul Mayeda Berges, based on Manzoor’s memoir Greetings from Bury Park. The film was made by Cornerstone Films, Bend It Films and Ingenious Media, distributed by Warner Bros. in the UK and New Line Cinema in the US. Cinematographer Ben Smithard shot the film on the Arri Alexa Mini at 2.8K; editor Justin Krish shaped its rhythm; the score was composed by A. R. Rahman, with Bruce Springsteen’s existing catalogue licensed for needle-drop sequences — a process that Springsteen personally approved. The film was filmed primarily in Luton over six weeks in 2018 and premiered at Sundance 2019.
